summary: The G and 2D shifts are a laser-power effect on one spot, not a sample difference. Both peaks red-shift linearly with power (G -1.80 cm-1 and 2D -5.14 cm-1 from 0.5 to 5 mW) while the Si reference stays put (+0.04 cm-1). That pattern fits local laser heating far better than doping. Doping would move G and 2D in the same direction, but here both go down, and the 2D/G area ratio stays at about 6.5. Strain cannot be ruled out, but one spot cannot separate it from heating or doping. Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for positions: it is the least heated, its zero-power extrapolation agrees with it to 0.2 cm-1 (G) and 0.1 cm-1 (2D), and its fit uncertainties are about 0.1 cm-1 or less. The 2 and 5 mW spectra are useful only as a power series for the heating correction.

observations.finding: G and 2D both red-shift monotonically with laser power; the Si 520 cm-1 reference does not shift.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fit + quadratic baseline. G centre 1581.30 (0.5 mW), 1580.63 (2 mW), 1579.50 (5 mW), +/-0.05-0.10 cm-1 stat. 2D centre 2669.52, 2666.41, 2664.38, +/-0.03-0.05. Si centre 520.86, 520.91, 520.91. Window and baseline-order variations move G by <=0.05 cm-1 and 2D by <=0.01 cm-1. Power slopes: G -0.40 cm-1/mW, 2D -1.08 cm-1/mW; 2D/G slope ratio 2.71 (3-point fit), 2.85 from endpoints.

observations.finding: Heating-equivalent temperature rise is inconsistent between G and 2D, and the 2D/G shift ratio (about 2.8) is above the single-layer temperature-coefficient ratio (about 2.1). Heating alone does not fully explain the data, and the zero-power reference is itself uncertain.
observations.evidence: Using Calizo et al. chi_G = -0.016 cm-1/K and chi_2D = -0.034 cm-1/K: dT_G = 1.80/0.016 = about 112 K and dT_2D = 5.14/0.034 = about 151 K for 5 mW relative to 0.5 mW. Taking the linear zero-power extrapolation (G 1581.47, 2D 2669.46) as the unheated reference gives about 11 K (G) and 2 K (2D) of heating already at 0.5 mW. Coefficients were measured with a temperature-controlled stage, not a focused laser.
observations.source: Calizo et al., Nano Lett. 7, 2645 (2007), arXiv:0708.1223, https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1223 (abstract gives chi_G and chi_2D)

observations.finding: No doping signature: the 2D/G intensity ratio does not change with power, and the shifts go the wrong way for doping.
observations.evidence: 2D/G height ratio 2.93, 2.99, 2.96 at 0.5, 2, 5 mW. Integrated-area ratio 6.71, 6.56, 6.42. Doping (either sign) shifts G and 2D in the same direction, and here both shift down together.

observations.finding: Peak widths broaden with power, which is consistent with heating-induced phonon damping, not with a change in defects or strain.
observations.evidence: G FWHM 13.9, 15.9, 18.0 cm-1 (about +30%); 2D FWHM 31.9, 34.7, 39.1 cm-1 (about +23%). Window and baseline variations change FWHM by about 0.5 cm-1, much less than the trend.

observations.finding: No measurable D band at any power, so the flake has no detectable defects.
observations.evidence: D-band Lorentzian height (1200-1500 cm-1 window, quadratic baseline): 6 +/- 8 counts at 0.5 mW, 22 +/- 17 at 2 mW, 141 +/- 514 at 5 mW. I(D)/I(G) is below about 0.02 at all powers.

observations.finding: Single-layer character is consistent with the spectrum but not independently established.
observations.evidence: Single-Lorentzian 2D with FWHM about 32 cm-1 at low power, 2D/G height about 3 and area ratio about 6.5. Thickness was not measured independently (no contrast or AFM data here).

observations.finding: The background is not a simple power scaling and differs between spectra, which can bias intensities and fitted widths.
observations.evidence: Local medians (counts) at 1100-1250 cm-1: 70 (0.5 mW), 783 (2 mW), 1740 (5 mW). At 3100-3199 cm-1: 170, 260, 3512. Ratio 5 mW/0.5 mW varies from about 7 to 25 across the spectrum. The 0.5 mW file contains exact zeros (minimum 0.0), suggesting different processing.

observations.finding: Si reference sits about +0.16 to +0.21 cm-1 above the nominal 520.7 cm-1, so absolute positions need a calibration offset of about -0.16 to -0.2 cm-1. The offset cancels in differences.
observations.evidence: Si centre 520.86 at 0.5 mW; 520.7 nominal Si first-order line (standard reference value, not sourced here).

observations.finding: Strain and charge can be separated only by correlating G and 2D across many spots; a single spot series cannot do it.
observations.evidence: Lee et al. report that correlation analysis of G and 2D separates strain from charge doping in SiO2-supported graphene, with strain ranging from -0.2% to 0.4% and hole doping after thermal treatment.
observations.source: Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012), arXiv:1209.0234, https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.0234 (abstract)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: undetermined (cannot be separated from heating or doping with this series)

properties.name: local_temperature_rise
properties.value: about 2-11 K at 0.5 mW; about 110-150 K at 5 mW relative to the zero-power extrapolation (uncertain)

properties.name: G_position_0.5mW
properties.value: 1581.30 +/- 0.10 cm-1 (before the approx. -0.16 cm-1 calibration offset)

properties.name: 2D_position_0.5mW
properties.value: 2669.52 +/- 0.05 cm-1 (before the approx. -0.16 cm-1 calibration offset)

caveats: The heating interpretation assumes the power-dependent shift is laser heating. The Si line does not shift, which argues against a substrate-wide temperature rise; the graphene's local temperature can exceed the substrate's, but that is an assumption not tested here.
The temperature coefficients (Calizo et al.) were measured on a stage-heated sample, so the converted temperatures are order-of-magnitude only.

The 2D/G shift ratio (2.7-2.85) is above the ~2.1 temperature-coefficient ratio and the ~2.2 strain ratio commonly quoted in the Raman literature. The strain ratio value is from memory and was not extracted from Mohiuddin et al. (arXiv:0812.1538, abstract only), so it is unverified.
The 3-point power slope has limited statistical power; the uncertainty on the 2D/G slope ratio is probably about +/-0.3 but was not formally propagated.

Fits use a Lorentzian plus a low-order polynomial. The broad power-dependent background is not well described by that model, and it may bias the fitted FWHM by a few cm-1 even though the centres are stable to about 0.05 cm-1.

The spectra were resampled to different point spacings (1.05, 1.01, 0.97 cm-1) with identical end points. Peak centres from fits are not affected at the reported precision, but native resolution should be checked against the instrument.
Acquisition order matters: if the 5 mW spectrum was taken before the 0.5 mW one, laser-induced adsorbate or annealing effects could produce the same drift, and the heating model would not apply.
questions_for_user: In what order were the three spectra taken? If the 5 mW spectrum came first, the drift could be laser-induced changes (adsorbates, annealing) rather than reversible heating. Please also confirm the laser power at the sample, not only at the source.

Were the spectra background-subtracted, and by what method? The 0.5 mW file has exact zeros, while 2 and 5 mW have a large, differently shaped background. Please give integration times and any dark or stray-light correction, because the intensities currently differ by factors of 7-25 in the background.

What is the SiO2 thickness (commonly 90 or 285-300 nm), and was the spectrum taken at the same spot each time? Interference enhancement changes the intensity ratios and can shift the apparent G and 2D centres.
Can you measure a power series down to about 0.1 mW, or a temperature series on a stage at 295 K, to pin the zero-power reference and the heating coefficients for this sample?
Do you have other spots with different G and 2D positions? Strain and doping can only be separated by correlating G against 2D across many spots (Lee et al., arXiv:1209.0234), not from one spot.

Is the 2D position near 2670 cm-1 at 532 nm expected for your substrate and calibration? Many unstrained SiO2-supported monolayers are reported near 2675-2680 cm-1 (commonly quoted value, not verified against a source here), so a 2D position near 2670 cm-1 at zero power would hint at tensile strain or residual doping that this series cannot resolve.

Lee, Ahn, Shim, Lee, Ryu, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012), arXiv:1209.0234, https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.0234 (G and 2D correlation separates strain from charge doping)
Mohiuddin et al., Phys. Rev. B 79, 205433 (2009), arXiv:0812.1538, https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1538 (uniaxial strain: G splits and both G and 2D red-shift; coefficients not extracted from abstract)
Mueller et al., arXiv:1703.09592, https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.09592 (found in search on arbitrary strain and doping in graphene via Raman; not read, cited only as further reading)
limits: One spot, three powers, one sample. The data cannot give absolute strain or doping values, and cannot determine strain sign independently of heating.
No polarization dependence, no anti-Stokes measurement, no independent thickness or contrast data, and no substrate-thickness information.
Literature numbers come from abstracts only; full texts were not read, so the uniaxial-strain coefficients and the Si temperature coefficient are not verified here.
Silicon 520.7 cm-1 nominal position is a standard reference value, not sourced from a paper in this session.
